points.description: States FALSE (the ISA is an abstraction provided by the CPU to the OS).

Justification: the ISA hides how functionality is implemented; the OS only sees instructions/registers mapped to functionality and does not know the implementation details (e.g. OS must be compiled for the specific ISA).
points.partial_credit: Give 0.75 if the justification is on the right track but vague, e.g. only says the OS uses the ISA/instructions without saying implementation is hidden.

rubric.notes: Full marks: FALSE with a justification that the ISA is an interface/abstraction whose implementation is hidden from the OS, in any wording. Part marks for FALSE with a vague or incomplete reason. No justification or answer of TRUE gives 0, since no correct justification means no marks.
